$comment: ONE FILE, TWO RUNNERS. __tests__/types/job.test.ts feeds these to isJobOverdue();
public.is_job_late(). If the TypeScript mirror and the SQL definition ever
disagree, one of the two suites fails on the case that separates them.
This improves on the entitlement precedent (GOLDEN_CASES in
api/tests/integration/test_billing_enforcement.py), where the two lists are kept
in step by a comment asking people to remember.
today is fixed at 2026-08-27 so the boundary cases mean something. Dates are
plain calendar dates on both sides -- no timezone conversion happens here,
which is the point: the caller supplies the day boundary.

cases.name: past due, on the floor, unshipped
past due, finished but not shipped -- delivery is the promise
past due, finished, only part shipped -- this is J-0021, the 7th job
past due but fully shipped -- delivered, so not late
past due but cancelled -- nobody is waiting
cancelled AFTER a partial shipment is still not late
due TODAY is not late -- the boundary is strict, you have until midnight
due yesterday IS late -- the other side of the same boundary
no due date -- we never promised, so it can never be late
no due date and long finished is still not late
